text:
Anya: Quick heads-up — GlacierCadence onboarding hit recurring tail latency spikes on long prompts this morning. Customer is nervous; renewal touchpoint in 4w. p95 jumped from ~2.4s to ~6.1s during their 10k-token tests. Can we triage and propose a low-risk perf recommendation? :thinking_face:
Sam: Ugh. Do we have breakdown (model, route, quant)?
Anya: They're on `gptx-3-8b` (hosted) via our default routing. No quantization yet. Traffic shows bursts 02:00–03:00 UTC from batch jobs.
Kai: Two quick levers: (1) suggest 8-bit quantized variant (compactpath-int8) — should cut token time ~25–35% for this arch; (2) introduce split routing: short/interactive -> hosted low-latency pool, long/batch -> dedicated high-throughput pool. Both are non-disruptive if we can canary.
Marco: Routing looks doable. We have spare dedicated capacity in us-west1 this week. Canary window could be 2 hours with 5% traffic.
Sam: How about quality/regression risk from int8? Any known failure modes for this model?
Kai: For gptx-3-8b int8 we've seen occasional token-level punctuation shifts on very edge prompts. Risk low for most instruction workloads. Recommend running a small eval set (10–20 prompts) — compare perplexity + our existing eval rubric. If pass, proceed.
Anya: Proposed plan:
1) Run quick eval (Sam/Kai) against GlacierCadence prompt set (10–20) — 1 business hour.
2) Canary compactpath-int8 on 5% traffic for 2 hours (Marco to schedule dedicated pool + route rule).
3) If metrics stable (p95 down, no quality regression), escalate to 50% for 24h then full swap.
4) Capture user feedback via weekly check-in; tie outcomes to renewal conversation.
Any objections?
Sam: Sounds good. I'll pull the prompt set and run eval now.
Marco: I can provision a small dedicated pool and push a routing rule: `if prompt_tokens > 1024 -> dedicated-compactpath-usw1`. Will post deploy bot updates.
deploy-bot: Provisioning job started (job_id: proj-4432). ETA ~8m.
Kai: Eval started. Quick script I used:
```
python3 eval_quality.py --model=gptx-3-8b-int8 --prompts=glacier_prompts.json --metrics=perplexity,exact_match
```
I'll paste results in thread when done.
Sam: One more ask — can we include a fallback policy so if dedicated pool CPU/GPU begins throttling we automatically fallback to hosted default? Don't want a single point of failure mid-canary.
Marco: Yes — I'll attach fallback route: on 5xx or latency > 8s -> fallback to hosted-default.
Anya: Great. Owners: Sam (eval + quality signoff), Marco (provision + routing + fallback), Kai (int8 watch + metric thresholds). I'll run customer check-in after first 2h canary.
Sam: Eval results: quality delta negligible on our rubric; perplexity +1.2% — within threshold.
Marco: Dedicated pool up and rule applied. Canary live at 05:12 UTC. Monitoring dashboards: https://console.redwood/obs/glaciercadence/1799994322
deploy-bot: Canary started. 5% traffic -> compactpath-int8 on dedicated-usw1.
Kai: Early telemetry: p95 down to 1.8s in canary cohort. No quality alerts so far.
Anya: I'll message the CSM and set renewal reassurance note. If everything stays good for 24h we recommend a staged rollout. Thanks team :raised_hands:
Sam: I'll capture the eval artifacts and add to the customer folder for audit.
Marco: I'll leave the fallback rule active and extend the canary to 50% in 2h if no regressions.
Anya: Closing loop: action items tracked in the CS playbook. Will ping again after 24h.
